title: Appendix B As An Executable Reference
notes: Open by telling students that this appendix is a reference appendix, but not a passive one. The useful reading strategy is to translate each named helper into a map between spaces. The API map gives the class an overview, while the deck will keep returning to the same question: what invariant would reveal a wrong convention?

title: Two Function Families: SO(3) And SE(3)
notes: Use this taxonomy slide to make the appendix useful as a reference without copying a package listing. The routines fall into four roles: rotation helpers, rigid-motion helpers, screw-coordinate helpers, and RobotLinks kinematics helpers. The point is to pair each function name with an input-output map and an invariant that would reveal a convention or implementation mistake.

title: Hat And Vee: Vectors Become Generators
notes: The hat operator is the bridge from coordinates to an infinitesimal generator. Stress that the matrix is not an arbitrary storage format. Its skew symmetry makes cross products appear as matrix multiplication, and that is why the same conversion sits under rotation exponentials, twist exponentials, and Jacobian columns. Vee is the sanity check that no independent coordinate was lost.

title: Exponential Maps Are The API's Mathematical Engine
notes: The appendix is short, so the exponential map does a lot of work. It turns an angular velocity generator into a finite rotation and a twist generator into a finite rigid motion. Explain that the API is organized around this engine: hat builds the generator, exponential moves to the group, and membership checks catch numerical or convention errors.

title: Homogeneous Coordinates: Points Translate, Vectors Do Not
notes: This is the slide for the most common hidden mistake in homogeneous coordinates. A point uses a trailing one because translating the frame changes the point's coordinates. A free vector uses a trailing zero because translation must not change direction or magnitude. Ask students to predict the effect before looking at the artifact; the bottom coordinate tells the story.

title: Twist Coordinates Encode Screw Geometry
notes: A twist is where the appendix becomes geometric rather than merely algebraic. The angular part names the screw axis direction. The linear part records the velocity induced at the origin, which is why the sign in v equals minus omega cross q matters. The class should leave this slide knowing what data a RobotLinks-style axis record must preserve.

title: Adjoint: Moving Twist Coordinates Between Frames
notes: Use the adjoint as a coordinate transport rule, not as a mysterious six-by-six block matrix. The same physical motion can be described in the body frame or in the space frame, but the numbers are different. This is the moment to connect API design with mathematical hygiene: a function name that omits the frame is not enough information for reliable robotics code.

title: RobotLinks: From Joint Axes To POE Kinematics
notes: RobotLinks is best introduced as a record of modeling decisions. It stores enough information to turn joint axes into twist coordinates, twist coordinates into a product-of-exponentials pose map, and the pose map into a spatial Jacobian. The displayed artifact is a reduced planar diagnostic from the notebook, not the full source SCARA chain; use it to inspect exponentials and Jacobian shape while naming the broader revolute and prismatic routine family.

title: Spatial Jacobian: Differentiating The POE Chain
notes: This slide completes the computational chain. The spatial Jacobian is not a fresh object unrelated to forward kinematics; it is the derivative of the product-of-exponentials map, expressed in a declared frame. The first column is already in the space frame, while later columns must be transported through earlier joint motions. That transport is exactly why the adjoint belongs in the API.

title: Reference Appendices Need Unit Tests
notes: Close by making the appendix's engineering lesson explicit. A reference appendix is valuable only if future readers can trust that its examples still run and still protect the intended geometry. The final sanity file checks transform structure, Jacobian dimensions, rank, manipulability, and artifact count. The visual storyboard checks that the three supporting figures are present and nonblank. That combination turns a reference into an audit trail.
